subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should Telegram `direct.<peer>.tools` and `toolsBySender` be treated as supported hard enforcement policy for DM sessions, and what precedence should it have against wildcard direct, topic, sender, group, and inherited policy layers?
rationale: The schema and types already expose the field, but enforcing it changes a security-sensitive runtime policy boundary and must preserve existing provider-scoped sender matching and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Support and enforce direct policy
options.body: Keep the config surface and implement a direct/DM-aware policy path with explicit precedence, regression tests, and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Retire the direct policy surface
options.body: Remove or doctor-migrate/document the accepted `direct.*.tools` shape so users do not rely on a non-enforced safety boundary.

options.title: Fold into broader binding policy design
options.body: Leave this blocked on a broader conversation/binding policy model if maintainers want one shared authorization contract instead of a Telegram-specific slice.

recommendation.title: Support and enforce direct policy
recommendation.body: Keep the config surface and implement a direct/DM-aware policy path with explicit precedence, regression tests, and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared policy resolver and scoped group-policy history make this the closest current security-boundary decision route.
